records.name: Pydantic AI core
records.version: VCS-derived; numeric release not resolved from pin

features_notes.durable_resume: Optional durable integrations/capabilities; an ordinary in-process Agent is not automatically durable.
features_notes.plugins: Capability and toolset composition, not necessarily a product extension marketplace.
features_notes.subagents: Agents can be called as tools; Coder self-delegation is separately recorded under Harness.
features_notes.otel: Instrumentation integrations exist; backend/export configuration was not runtime-tested.

dims.loop: Typed graph transitions around model request, tool handling, validation and suspended state.
dims.providers: Provider adapters normalize model requests/results; retry data survives optional durable boundaries.
dims.tools: Typed tools/toolsets, MCP and approval-required wrappers.
dims.context: Messages and capabilities compose context policy; coding defaults belong to the separate Harness package.
dims.state: Optional Temporal/Durable capability integrations; application must select storage/worker architecture.
dims.safety: Tool approval/retry/validation contracts; core typing alone does not isolate effects.
dims.extensibility: Capabilities, model adapters, toolsets and typed dependencies.
dims.multi_agent: Agent-as-tool composition; Harness adds a specific delegate workflow.
dims.surfaces: In-process Python API and integration packages.
dims.observability: Structured events/instrumentation; no live backend tested.

records.one_liner: A typed agent framework with explicit durable integrations and a separately packaged coding harness.
key_insights: Typed model/tool graph execution is separate from the newer coding Harness package.
Durable integrations require explicit capability and backend selection; ordinary Agent runs remain in-process.

records.name: Pydantic AI Harness

features_notes.durable_resume: StepPersistence records events/effects and settled snapshots, defaulting to an in-memory store; started effects may become unknown_after_crash.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Optional BubblewrapSandbox wraps the workspace with network denial; plain LocalWorkspace is not isolated.
features_notes.compaction: Coder defaults to clearing old tool results; exported summarizers are optional capabilities.
features_notes.mcp_client: Available through the underlying Pydantic AI toolset layer.
features_notes.approvals: Inherited approval mechanism; Coder shell configuration does not itself imply approval gating.
features_notes.skills: Capability surface exported; not every capability is enabled by Coder.

dims.loop: Coder capability configures an ordinary Pydantic Agent; graph/model loop remains core-owned.
dims.providers: Underlying Pydantic provider abstraction and model capability composition.
dims.tools: Workspace-bound files/grep/shell, bounded tool results, repaired arguments and delegate tools.
dims.context: Instruction/repository context plus default old-result clearing; optional summarizing capabilities.
dims.state: Opt-in event/effect ledger and settled-step snapshots; unresolved effects require recovery decisions.
dims.safety: Optional bubblewrap workspace; default shell permits commands and may outlive the agent run.
dims.extensibility: Explicit capability bundle with interchangeable workspace, persistence, context and tool policy.
dims.multi_agent: Coder can spawn fresh instances of its bound agent with inherited capabilities.
dims.surfaces: Python package for embeddable coding agents; convenience coder agent factory.
dims.observability: Core instrumentation plus explicit persistence records; alpha contracts require migration tolerance.

records.one_liner: A real composable coding harness layered over Pydantic AI, with optional persistence and workspace isolation.
key_insights: Coder assembles capabilities onto an ordinary Pydantic Agent rather than introducing another model loop.
StepPersistence defaults to memory and preserves unresolved-effect ambiguity after crashes.
Workspace isolation and richer summarizers are optional capabilities, not universal Coder defaults.

records.name: smolagents

features_notes.durable_resume: Inspected save() exports agent code/config/UI; it is not a running-step checkpoint or effect journal.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Local Python evaluator is explicitly not a security sandbox; optional remote executors provide distinct boundaries.
features_notes.subagents: Managed agents exist, but the inspected remote CodeAgent executor path rejects them.
features_notes.mcp_client: Optional MCP tool conversion is documented by the first-party repository.
features_notes.hooks: Step callbacks rather than an unrestricted product plugin system.
features_notes.web_ui: Optional/exported demo UI; not a complete host platform.

dims.loop: MultiStepAgent loop with optional planning, bounded steps and final-answer validation; code and tool-call variants.
dims.providers: Provider adapters and optional integrations documented by the repository.
dims.tools: Python code execution or structured tools; thread-pool execution for eligible tool-call batches.
dims.context: Step memory and planning prompts; general durable compaction not established in inspected paths.
dims.state: In-process run state; export save() serializes agent definition, not a live execution checkpoint.
dims.safety: Restricted local evaluator is not a sandbox; Docker/E2B/Modal/Blaxel alternatives require selection.
dims.extensibility: Tools, executor subclasses, model wrappers and step callbacks.
dims.multi_agent: Managed-agent calls; remote CodeAgent execution currently rejects managed agents.
dims.surfaces: Python SDK, CLI/example and optional Gradio-style UI surfaces.
dims.observability: Step logs/memory/callbacks; runtime failure recovery not independently tested.

records.one_liner: A compact code/tool agent library; remote isolation and managed-agent composition have concrete compatibility limits.
key_insights: CodeAgent and structured-tool agents share a compact step loop with replaceable executors.
The local Python evaluator is explicitly not a security sandbox; inspected remote execution rejects managed agents.
save() exports an agent definition, not a checkpoint of running work.

records.name: Microsoft Agent Framework

features_notes.durable_resume: Workflow checkpoints include topology, executor/edge state and pending input; ordinary harness defaults differ.
features_notes.approvals: Requires AgentSession for persistence; standing rules are not bound to tool implementation identity.
features_notes.subagents: Agent-as-tool cannot propagate child approvals; approval-capable delegation should use Workflow.
features_notes.os_sandbox: File-access controls are not proof of an OS isolation backend.
features_notes.plan_mode: Harness mode capability, not asserted as a fully identical product plan mode.
features_notes.agents_md: Repository instructions are configurable; exact file-discovery parity not established.

dims.loop: Model agent loop plus separate repeat-until/judge harness loop and Pregel-style workflow supersteps.
dims.providers: Provider-neutral framework interfaces; this chapter does not assert Python/.NET feature parity.
dims.tools: Tools, optional file access, skills and background/delegate capabilities.
dims.context: History, per-request or post-run compaction, todo/mode and scoped file-memory capabilities.
dims.state: Workflow checkpoints persist topology, committed state, fan-in and pending input; commit/discard boundary explicit.
dims.safety: Opt-in approvals with standing rules and session storage; no general OS sandbox proved here.
dims.extensibility: Factory assembles capabilities; workflows/executors/edges provide separate orchestration extension layer.
dims.multi_agent: Workflow graphs with fan-in and checkpoints; direct child-tool approval propagation has a documented limit.
dims.surfaces: Python embedding and workflow libraries; broader C# project exists but not deeply audited.
dims.observability: Event/checkpoint records; no backend export or failover runtime experiment performed.

records.one_liner: A broad framework with a concrete coding harness and checkpointed workflow layer; capability selection changes guarantees.
key_insights: Coding harness assembly, the model/tool loop and checkpointed workflows are distinct layers.
Workflow checkpoints preserve committed executor state and pending input across supersteps.
Direct agent-as-tool delegation cannot propagate child approvals; workflows supply the richer coordination boundary.

records.name: Letta Code

features_notes.durable_resume: Local transcripts plus owned execution/recovery checkpoints; effects and checkpoint writes are not one atomic transaction.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Optional bwrap/Seatbelt backend; wrapper can return no backend, so verify host policy before relying on isolation.
features_notes.worktrees: Inspected worktrees isolate memory-worker changes; not a claim that every coding delegate gets a worktree.
features_notes.in_process_sdk: Reusable internal components and separate SDK surface; no independent stability guarantee established.
features_notes.subagents: Local headless subprocess or remote dispatch; new child sessions do not inherit memory semantics universally.
features_notes.skills: Bundled skills included in the inspected package; discovery/compatibility semantics not deeply audited.
features_notes.mcp_client: Product integration present; server interoperability not tested.

dims.loop: ProviderTurnExecutor normalizes model streaming and approval stops; headless host dispatches permitted tools.
dims.providers: Local PiStreamAdapter uses pi-ai; this is not evidence of pi-agent-core or pi-durable lineage.
dims.tools: Host tool execution with permission classification, approval requests and before/after evidence checkpoints.
dims.context: Sliding-window compaction plus committed Git-backed memory compiled separately into prompts.
dims.state: Pi-session-entry JSONL transcripts and claimed execution/recovery ownership; ambiguous external effects remain possible.
dims.safety: Permissions and optional OS backend; missing backend and broad-read policy require attention.
dims.extensibility: Mods expose tools/providers/commands/UI/events/permissions; hooks can participate in checks.
dims.multi_agent: Headless local children or remote jobs; memory workers use private Git worktrees with conflict retention.
dims.surfaces: Integrated CLI/headless product with internal executors and remote recovery surfaces.
dims.observability: Transcripts, execution checkpoints and recovery evidence; no independent crash/security test performed.

records.one_liner: A current local/provider coding runtime with Git-backed memory, mods and recovery machinery built partly on pi-ai.

source_repos.scope: 12-file landing repository; server implementation not assessable from this snapshot

key_insights: The current TypeScript product uses pi-ai provider streaming; this does not establish pi-agent-core or pi-durable lineage.
Git-backed memory and sliding-window conversation compaction are separate mechanisms.
Recovery evidence tracks tool boundaries, while optional sandbox backends and memory-worker worktrees have limited scopes.
